# Rushan Haque

He designs and builds custom business websites, online stores, export catalogues and web applications from scratch, for businesses across India and abroad (clients in India, Saudi Arabia, Poland and Nepal), and looks after them after launch.

# Common questions

Q: Do you work with clients outside India?
A: Yes. Clients so far are in India, Saudi Arabia, Poland and Nepal, and most of the export businesses I build for sell to buyers in dozens of countries. Everything runs smoothly over calls, WhatsApp and email.

Q: What does a project include?
A: The whole lifecycle: discovery, design, development, hosting and handover. You get a site that is fast on phones, set up for search, and simple for your team to update.

Q: Can you redesign the website I already have?
A: Yes. We start from what works on your current site, keep what you have earned in search, and rebuild the rest around your products and buyers.

Q: What happens after launch?
A: I stay in touch long after the site goes live — updates, improvements, new pages, and a person to call when something needs doing.

Q: Do you build online stores and software too?
A: Yes — e-commerce stores, digital catalogues, inventory systems, CRMs and tools like Mailwright. If your team does it by hand today, it can probably be software tomorrow.

# Every guide, service and area page

## Hire a website developer, wherever you are
https://www.rushanhaque.in/hire-website-developer

One designer and developer for your whole website, from the first call to launch and after, working remotely with businesses in India and abroad.

- Based in: India (IST, UTC+5:30)
- Works with: Businesses in India and abroad, fully remote
- Languages: English, Hindi and French
- Builds with: Next.js, React and cloud hosting

### One developer, start to launch
When you hire me, the person on your first call is the person who designs the pages, writes the code, sets up hosting and launches the site. There is no account manager in between and nothing is lost in a hand-over.
Every website is designed for the business it serves and built from scratch, not assembled from a template, so it loads fast, reads well on a phone and has a structure search engines understand.

### Working across countries and time zones
- Written updates: Progress is shared in writing and on a live preview link, so you can follow the work in your own time zone.
- Calls when you need them: Video or phone calls in English, Hindi or French, booked at a time that suits you.
- You own everything: The domain, the hosting account and the code are in your name once the project is complete.
- Support after launch: Fixes, updates and new pages after the site is live, from the same person who built it.

### What you can hire me for
Business and company websites, e-commerce stores, product catalogues for exporters, landing pages for campaigns, web applications such as dashboards and booking tools, and redesigns of sites that have stopped working for the business.

### How a remote project runs
1. Tell me what the website has to do: By email, WhatsApp or the contact form. A few lines is enough to start.
2. A call about your business: Who your customers are, what they need to find, and what a good result looks like.
3. A written plan: The pages, features and timeline agreed in writing before any work starts.
4. Design, build and launch: You approve the design first, review the build on a live preview link, and the site goes live once you are happy with it.

### What to check before you hire any developer
- Live sites, not mock-ups: Ask for websites that are online now and open them on your own phone.
- Ownership: Make sure the domain, hosting and code will be yours, not rented from the developer.
- Speed and search: A good build is fast on mobile data and ships with a sitemap, structured data and clean headings.
- Who does the work: Find out whether the person you speak to is the person who builds the site, or whether it is passed on.

### Questions
Q: Can I hire you if my business is outside India?
A: Yes. Projects run remotely over email, WhatsApp and video calls, with a live preview link, so clients can work with me from any country.

Q: Are you a freelancer or an agency?
A: A freelancer. I design and build every website myself, and work with trusted partners only for services such as ad campaigns or social media management, while staying your single point of contact.

Q: How long does it take to build a website?
A: A landing page usually takes one to two weeks, a business website two to four weeks, and an e-commerce store or catalogue four to eight weeks.

Q: Who owns the website when it is finished?
A: You do. The domain, the hosting account and the code are yours once the project is complete.

Q: Will my website show up on Google and in AI answers?
A: Every site is built for search: fast pages, clear headings, structured data and a sitemap, submitted to Google Search Console, and written so AI assistants can quote it. Rankings also depend on reviews and links from other sites, and I help you build those.

Q: What do you need from me to start?
A: A short description of your business and what the website has to do. Content such as photos and text can come later, and I can help write it.


## Website developer in Moradabad
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-developer-in-moradabad

Custom-coded websites and web applications, developed, hosted and supported end to end by a full-stack developer based in Moradabad.

- Based in: Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
- Builds: Websites, stores and web apps
- Approach: Coded from scratch, no page builders

### A web developer, not just a template
A website developer turns a design into a working site: the code, the payments, the forms, the database, the hosting and the speed. Every site here is written from scratch, without themes or drag-and-drop builders, so it does exactly what your business needs and nothing slows it down.
I am a full-stack developer based in Moradabad, so the same person plans the project, writes the code, puts it online and supports it after launch.

### What gets developed
- Business websites: Fast, mobile-first sites that explain what you do and turn visitors into calls and enquiries.
- E-commerce stores: Product pages, cart and checkout with Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree or Stripe.
- Web applications: Portals, dashboards and internal tools built around how your business works.
- Export catalogues: Searchable product catalogues and enquiry forms for overseas buyers.
- Speed and fixes: Slow or broken sites made fast and reliable, including sites I did not build.
- Integrations: Payment gateways, WhatsApp enquiries, email, spreadsheets and the tools you already use.

### How it is built
- Modern, fast code: Pages are rendered on the server, so they load quickly on mobile data and search engines can read every word.
- Mobile first: Designed and tested on phones first, because that is where most of your customers will see it.
- Search built in: Clean structure, structured data, sitemaps and Core Web Vitals, from day one rather than as an add-on.
- Hosting and handover: Hosting, domain and email set up and handed over, so the site stays yours.

### How a project runs
1. Tell me what it has to do: On WhatsApp, by email or through the form. A few lines is enough.
2. A 30-minute call: In Hindi or English, about the business and the people it serves.
3. A written quote: Scope, cost and timeline in writing, before any work starts.
4. Build and launch: You approve the design first; the site is handed over once it is live.

### Questions
Q: Is a website developer different from a website designer?
A: A designer decides how a site looks and works; a developer builds it in code and puts it online. I do both, so one person carries the project from the first sketch to the live site.

Q: Do you build with WordPress or with code?
A: With code, by default. WordPress is used only when a project genuinely needs it, usually when a non-technical team has to publish often.

Q: Can you take over development of an existing website?
A: Yes. After a look at the code and the hosting, I can fix it, speed it up, add features or rebuild it the right way.

Q: Do you develop web applications as well as websites?
A: Yes: portals, dashboards, booking and enquiry systems and internal tools, built around how your business works.

Q: Do you work with clients outside Moradabad?
A: Yes. Most work happens remotely, for clients across India and abroad, with calls in Hindi or English.

## What does a website cost in Moradabad?
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-cost-in-moradabad

What actually decides the quote, how long each kind of site takes, and the running costs nobody mentions until later.

- Pricing: A fixed, written quote
- Decided by: What the site has to do
- Running costs: Domain, hosting, email

### Every website is quoted on what it has to do
A website is priced by its scope, not by the number of pages alone. A one-page site, a business website, an online store and a custom web application are different pieces of work, and every project gets a written quote with a timeline before any work starts.
What you need | Usually takes
One-page site or landing page | 1–2 weeks
Business website, 5 to 10 pages | 2–4 weeks
E-commerce store or export catalogue | 4–8 weeks
Custom web application or portal | Scoped per project
Timelines depend on scope, ready content and how quickly feedback comes back.

### Five things that change the price
- Distinct page types: Ten pages built from one layout cost less than five pages that each need their own design.
- Products and catalogues: A catalogue of 40 products is a different job from one of 4,000. Bulk import, filters and specification tables add work.
- Payments and accounts: Online payments through Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree or Stripe, customer logins, order tracking and shipping rules each add building and testing.
- Content: If your photos and text are ready, the project moves faster and costs less. Writing and product photography add to the scope.
- Languages and markets: A second language, more than one currency, or pages aimed at buyers in other countries add design and SEO work.

### What a website costs every year
The build is a one-time project. These are the recurring costs, paid to the providers directly. Register the domain and hosting in your own name, so the site always belongs to you.
Running cost | What it is
Domain name (.com or .in) | Renewed every year with your registrar
Hosting | Depends on traffic; a small, fast site costs very little
Business email | Per person, per month, for example Google Workspace
Changes and new features | Quoted as a small project when you need them

### Why the cheapest website often costs more
Very cheap websites are usually a template with your logo on it. They tend to load slowly, look like hundreds of other sites, and are rarely set up to be found on Google. Many are rebuilt within a year or two, so the business pays twice.
That said, sometimes a template or a website builder is the right call. If you need a simple page this week and have no budget, start there, and invest in a proper build once the business needs it.

### How to get an exact price
1. Tell me what the site has to do: On WhatsApp, by email or through the form. A few lines is enough to start.
2. A 30-minute call: To understand the business, the customers and what the website has to achieve.
3. A written quote: Scope, price and timeline in writing, before any work begins.
4. Design, build, launch: You see the design before it is built, and the site is handed over once it is live.

### Questions
Q: How much does a website cost in Moradabad?
A: It depends on what the site has to do: a one-page site, a business website, an online store and a custom application are priced very differently. Tell me what you need and you get a fixed, written quote before any work starts.

Q: What makes an e-commerce website cost more?
A: The number of products, online payments, customer accounts, shipping rules and integrations. Platforms like Shopify cost less to start but charge monthly fees and transaction costs.

Q: Is there a monthly fee for the website?
A: The website itself is a one-time project. The recurring costs are your domain, hosting and email, paid to those providers directly.

Q: Why do website quotes vary so much?
A: Because a website can mean a single page or a full online store with payments, accounts and thousands of products. Compare quotes by what is included: design, the number of page types, content, SEO setup, speed, and who owns the domain and code.

Q: How long does it take to build a website?
A: A landing page usually takes 1 to 2 weeks, a business website 2 to 4 weeks, and an e-commerce store or catalogue 4 to 8 weeks. Ready content and quick feedback keep it on the shorter side.

Q: Will my website rank on Google?
A: Every site is built with technical SEO in place: fast pages, clean structure, structured data and Search Console. Ranking for competitive searches also takes content and time.


## Websites for Moradabad exporters and manufacturers
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-for-exporters-moradabad

Catalogues buyers can search, enquiries that arrive with item codes, and pages that rank where your buyers are.

- Built for: Exporters, manufacturers and buying houses
- Materials: Brass, copper, iron, aluminium, wood
- Live examples: Taif, Aurelio, Casa&Crop, Erfolg Living

### Your buyer looks you up before the trade fair
Moradabad ships metalware and handicrafts to buyers all over the world. Many of those buyers now shortlist suppliers online before they visit a fair like IHGF Delhi or Ambiente Frankfurt, and they check you again after meeting you. A PDF catalogue and a three-page website do not survive that shortlist.
A good export website does three jobs: it proves you are a real manufacturer, it shows your range in a way a buyer can search, and it turns a visit into a specific enquiry.

### What an export website needs
- A real product catalogue: Every product gets its own page with photos, material, finish, dimensions and an item code, so a buyer can find one piece instead of scrolling a PDF.
- Collections and filters: The range grouped the way buyers think, by collection, material, finish and room, with filters that narrow it down.
- Enquiries with item codes: A short form or an enquiry list that sends the exact products a buyer wants, straight to your inbox or WhatsApp.
- Proof of the factory: Your process, capacity and materials, the markets you ship to, and certifications such as SMETA or BSCI where you hold them.
- Pages that rank abroad: Product and collection pages that search engines can read, fast loading on overseas connections, and structured data for Google and AI assistants.
- New collections without a rebuild: Adding a season’s range should be quick, so it is planned for from the start.

### Export websites already live
- Taif International: Metal and wooden handicraft manufacturer in Moradabad, exporting to 42 countries. Nine collections, from wooden and copper products to barware and religious supplies.
- Aurelio: The metal and wood atelier of AF International: furniture, lighting, urns and objets made by hand in Moradabad since 2008.
- Casa and Crop: Manufacturers and exporters of home metalware in brass, copper and steel, shipping from Moradabad to 34 countries.
- Erfolg Living: Handmade luxury metalwork: artisan copper bathtubs, sinks, lighting and furniture.
- Velora International: A trade atelier hand-raising heirloom objects in brass, bronze, copper and silver since 2021. The site is being finished.

### How an export site comes together
1. Your range and your buyers: We go through the collections, the item codes and the markets you sell to.
2. Catalogue structure: Collections, filters and product pages planned around how buyers search.
3. Design and build: A site that looks like the quality of what you make, and loads fast everywhere.
4. Search setup and launch: Sitemaps, structured data and Google Search Console in place from day one.
Timelines depend on the size of the catalogue and the features it needs; you get a written quote before work starts.

### Questions
Q: Can you upload our full product catalogue?
A: Yes. Products can be brought in from a spreadsheet with item codes, materials, finishes and dimensions, then organised into collections and filters.

Q: Do you build B2B websites that do not show prices?
A: Yes. Most export sites show the range and collect enquiries instead of selling online. Buyers request a quote for the item codes they want.

Q: Can the website be in more than one language?
A: Yes. Key pages can be added in the languages of the markets you sell to, set up so that Google shows the right version in each country.

Q: Will a website bring us overseas buyers?
A: A website does not replace fairs or buying agents, but it is where buyers check you after meeting you and where new ones find you through search. It is built to rank for your products and to make enquiring easy.

Q: Do you work with exporters outside Moradabad?
A: Yes. The studio is in Moradabad and works with manufacturers across India, remotely or in person nearby.


## Website builder or web designer: which do you need?
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-builder-vs-web-designer

An honest comparison of website makers and custom websites: cost, speed, SEO and who owns what.

- Website builder: Monthly fee, a template, you rent it
- Custom website: One-time build, your design, you own it

### What a website builder is
A website builder, also called a website maker, is a subscription service such as Wix, Squarespace, Hostinger Website Builder or Shopify. You pick a template, drag in your content and publish. The platform hosts the site, and you pay every month or year for as long as it stays online.
A web designer builds a website for your business specifically: the structure, the design, the content and the code. You pay for the build once, then for hosting and any changes.

### Side by side
 | Website builder | Custom website
Cost to start | Low: a subscription | Higher: a one-time build
Cost over three years | Subscriptions, add-on apps and transaction fees add up | Mostly hosting and the domain
Design | A template shared with many other sites | Designed for your business and your customers
Speed | Often heavy, with scripts you cannot remove | Built lean, fast on mobile networks
SEO | The basics, with limited control over structure | Full control: structure, speed, structured data
Ownership | You rent the platform; leaving usually means rebuilding | Your code and content, on hosting in your name
Who does the work | You do | A professional does it with you

### When a builder is the right choice
- You have almost no budget: A builder gets you online for the price of a subscription. That is better than no website.
- You need a page this week: For a simple page with your details, a template is fast.
- You are testing an idea: Prove the idea first, then invest in a proper build once it works.
- You want to run a small shop yourself: Shopify is a strong choice if you want to manage everything yourself and the monthly fee plus transaction costs suit you.

### When to hire a web designer
- The website has to win customers: Not just exist, but turn visitors into calls, enquiries and orders.
- Buyers compare you with competitors: Exporters, manufacturers and service firms are judged on their website before the first call.
- You need to be found on Google: Ranking in your city or industry needs control over speed, structure and content.
- A template cannot do what you need: Product catalogues, booking, customer portals or anything specific to how you work.
- You have outgrown your builder: Slow pages, rising subscriptions, or a design that no longer fits the business.

### The middle path
Plenty of good businesses start on a builder and move to a custom website once they grow. If your site is on Wix, Squarespace or WordPress today, a redesign can move your content across and keep your Google rankings with proper redirects.

### Questions
Q: What is the best website maker in India?
A: For a do-it-yourself site, the common choices are Wix, Hostinger Website Builder and Squarespace, and Shopify for online stores. For a business that needs to stand out, rank and turn visitors into customers, a custom website built by a web designer is usually the better long-term investment.

Q: Is Wix good for SEO?
A: Wix covers the SEO basics, and Wix sites can rank. The limits are page weight and control over how pages are built, which matter more in competitive searches.

Q: Can you move my website from Wix or WordPress?
A: Yes. The content is moved across, old addresses are redirected so rankings are kept, and the new site is built to be faster.

Q: Is a custom website more expensive than a builder?
A: It costs more to start, because it is built for you. Builders charge a subscription every month for as long as the site is online, plus apps and transaction fees, so over a few years the gap is often smaller than it looks.

Q: Can I edit a custom website myself?
A: Yes, where that is part of the brief. Content that changes often gets an admin panel; content that changes twice a year does not need one.


## How to get a website made for your business
https://www.rushanhaque.in/how-to-get-a-website-made

Everything to sort out before, during and after a website is built, in the order it happens.

- For: Business owners in India
- Read time: About 6 minutes
- Also in: हिंदी

### Start with what the website has to do
Before colours or pages, write down the one or two things the website must achieve. Bring in enquiries on WhatsApp, sell products online, show export buyers a catalogue, or let parents find admission details. Every later decision follows from this.
Then list who it is for: local customers searching on their phones, buyers abroad comparing suppliers, or patients looking for timings. A website built for its real visitors does far more than one built to look impressive.

### What to prepare before you call anyone
- Your business details: Name, address, phone, WhatsApp, timings and the areas you serve, written exactly the same way everywhere.
- Photos: Real photos of your work, products, shop or team. Phone photos in good daylight are better than stock images.
- The words: A few lines about the business, each service or product, and the questions customers ask most. A designer can help write the rest.
- Examples you like: Two or three websites you like, and why. It saves a lot of back and forth.

### Domain, hosting and email
The domain is your address, such as yourbusiness.in or yourbusiness.com. Register it in your own name with a registrar you can log in to, so it always belongs to you.
Hosting is where the website lives. A small, fast site costs very little to host. Business email such as you@yourbusiness.in is set up separately, usually through Google Workspace or Zoho.
Thing | What to check
Domain | Registered in your name, with the login details in your hands
Hosting | Fast in India, with SSL (the padlock) included
Email | On your own domain, not a free address
Code | Handed over to you once the project is paid for

### Choosing who builds it
You can use a website builder like Wix or Shopify yourself, hire an agency, or work with a freelance designer and developer. Builders are quick to start but charge monthly and are harder to rank. Agencies cost more and pass work between people. A freelancer who designs and codes keeps it in one pair of hands.

### Questions to ask before you pay
- Is it built from scratch or from a template?: Both can work, but you should know which one you are paying for.
- Will I own the domain, hosting and code?: The answer should be yes.
- How fast will it load on a phone?: Ask to see a past site tested on Google PageSpeed Insights.
- What is included for Google?: Page titles, structured data, a sitemap, Search Console and help with your Google Business Profile.
- What does it cost after launch?: Domain, hosting and email every year, and how changes are charged.

### After the website goes live
1. Submit it to Google: Add the site to Google Search Console and submit the sitemap, so Google finds every page.
2. Set up your Google Business Profile: Link it to the website. This is what puts you on Google Maps for searches nearby.
3. Ask customers for reviews: Reviews on your Google Business Profile are one of the strongest local signals.
4. Keep it current: Add new work, products and answers to common questions. Pages that stay useful keep ranking.

### Questions
Q: How do I get a website made for my business?
A: Decide what the website has to do, and prepare your business details, photos and a few lines of text. Register a domain in your own name, then choose a website builder, an agency or a freelance designer, and get a written quote before work starts.

Q: How long does it take to make a website?
A: A landing page usually takes one to two weeks, a business website two to four weeks, and an online store or catalogue four to eight weeks, depending on how ready the content is.

Q: Do I need to know coding to get a website?
A: No. A designer and developer handles the building. You only need to explain the business and approve the design.

Q: Can I get a website made remotely?
A: Yes. Projects can run entirely over calls, WhatsApp and email, with a live preview link to follow the work from anywhere in India.

Q: How will customers find my website on Google?
A: Through a fast, well-structured site submitted to Google Search Console, a Google Business Profile linked to it, customer reviews, and links from directories and other sites.

01 The search The search box is moving A growing share of questions that used to produce ten blue links now produce a written answer with a handful of citations.
02 What GEO What GEO work involves Structured data 01 Schema.org markup describing the business, its services, its location and its reviews as machine-readable facts rather than prose an assistant has to infer from. Answer-shaped content 02 Direct answers placed high on the page, in the 40-to-60 word block an assistant can lift whole. Crawler access 03 GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and the rest explicitly permitted in robots.txt. Server-rendered content 04 AI crawlers largely do not execute JavaScript. llms.txt 05 A plain-language summary written for machines, giving an assistant a clean account of who you are and what you do. Entity consistency 06 The same name, address, phone and description everywhere, so an assistant can be confident two mentions are the same business.
03 Why it Why it is worth doing now SEO is thirty years old and every competitive term has someone defending it.
04 Questions What clients ask 01 What is Generative Engine Optimization? GEO is optimising a site so that AI assistants — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and others — cite it as a source when answering questions. 02 Is GEO different from SEO? It builds on SEO and adds to it. Fast, crawlable, well-structured pages help both. 03 How do I get cited by ChatGPT? Allow OpenAI's crawlers in robots.txt, publish content that answers real questions directly and early, mark the facts up in schema so they can be attributed, and make sure the content exists in the HTML rather than appearing after JavaScript runs.

## Website redesign
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-redesign

Website redesign that starts by diagnosing what is actually costing you — speed, mobile layout, structure or search visibility — instead of restyling and hoping.

Home Website redesign S Service Discipline Redesign & rebuild Starts with Diagnosis, not a mockup Scope Targeted pass or full rebuild A redesign that begins with a diagnosis rather than a mockup. Start a project See the work
01 Redesign is Redesign is usually the wrong first question “The site looks dated” is rarely why a site is not working.
02 What the What the diagnosis looks at Speed 01 Real load time on a mid-range phone over mobile data, not a desktop score. Mobile behaviour 02 Whether the layout works on a phone or merely fits on one. Search health 03 Indexing, canonicals, redirects, structured data, and whether the site is even eligible to rank. Structure 04 Whether a first-time visitor can find what they came for without guessing. Conversion path 05 Whether it is obvious what to do next, and whether the way to do it works. Content 06 Whether the copy answers the questions people arrive with.
03 Two ways Two ways it goes Sometimes the diagnosis says the foundation is sound and three specific things are wrong.
04 Questions What clients ask 01 How do I know if I need a redesign or just fixes? Look at the diagnosis before deciding. If the site loads reasonably, is indexed, and works on a phone, targeted fixes will usually get you most of the way. 02 Will I lose my Google rankings if I redesign? Only if the migration is done carelessly. Rankings are lost when URLs change without redirects, when content is cut, or when the new site blocks crawling. 03 Can you redesign without changing our branding? Yes. Plenty of redesigns keep the identity entirely and change only the things that were costing money.

## Website speed optimization
https://www.rushanhaque.in/website-speed-optimization

Website speed optimization and Core Web Vitals fixes, measured on real mid-range phones over mobile data — how your visitors actually load the site.

Home Website speed optimization S Service Discipline Performance engineering Measured on Mid-range phone, mobile data Targets LCP, INP, CLS Speed work measured the way visitors experience it: a mid-range Android phone on mobile data, not a desktop test on office broadband. Start a project See the work
01 The score The score is not the point A perfect score from a testing tool run on a fast desktop connection tells you very little about the person trying to load your site on a bus.
02 Where the Where the time usually goes Images 01 Almost always the largest cost. Uncompressed, wrongly sized, in outdated formats, and loaded before anything the visitor can see. JavaScript 02 Frameworks and plugins loaded for features a page never uses. Render-blocking resources 03 Stylesheets and scripts in the head that stop the page painting until they arrive. Fonts 04 Custom fonts that block text from appearing, or swap in late and shift the layout under the reader. Third-party tags 05 Analytics, chat widgets, pixels and embeds, each adding a connection to somewhere you do not control. Server response 06 Slow hosting or an uncached backend that delays the very first byte, before the browser can start on anything else.
03 What Core What Core Web Vitals actually measure LCP — Largest Contentful Paint 01 How long until the main thing appears. Usually an image or headline. INP — Interaction to Next Paint 02 How quickly the page responds when someone taps. CLS — Cumulative Layout Shift 03 How much the page moves while loading. The reason you tap the wrong thing on a news site.
04 Questions What clients ask 01 Why is my website slow? Most often images that are far larger than the space they are shown in, followed by JavaScript the page does not need. 02 Does site speed affect Google rankings? Yes, though less dramatically than often claimed. 03 What is a good Core Web Vitals score? LCP under 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 milliseconds, CLS under 0.1 — measured on real mobile visits, not a lab test.
